cover.title: Recoil Report — Jul 20 Call
cover.subtitle: Proposal walkthrough → Phase 1 chatbot confirmed at $1,500, routed to the sales manager. The real substance: Todd generated the Phase 1 data model himself and opened a wide Phase 2+ surface.
cover.meta: Call: Jul 20, 2026 · ~35 min · phone (Todd en route to airport)

loadBearingQuote.text: Let's start with this chatbot. And just keep it simple, routed to the sales manager. Then take it from there — getting the rest of the team involved in the technology is going to be a huge pain in the ass.

callWalk.label: Open
callWalk.title: Personal catch-up
callWalk.body: Caught up first (date night, family, Zach's job search). Todd joined from the car heading to the airport — warm, low-friction, ready to move.

callWalk.label: Walkthrough
callWalk.title: The proposal, in ~3 minutes
callWalk.body: Zach walked the simplified page: chatbot first, route to the sales manager, rent Tidio on WordPress → SugarCRM, three tiers. Phase 1 = 3 sessions / ~1 week / $1,500. Todd tracked it easily.

callWalk.label: Turn
callWalk.title: Todd generates the Phase 1 data model
callWalk.body: Todd's move: take the product-development / application-discovery form the reps use and build a 'light version' as the chatbot's capture fields — contact info + application + resin currently in use. Zach's guardrail: keep required fields minimal to avoid form-fatigue; capture the 1–2 must-haves, not the whole form.

callWalk.label: Reframe
callWalk.title: Buyers are engineers, not budgets
callWalk.body: Todd: inquiries are almost always engineers; budget isn't the driver (occasionally a purchasing manager). CS reps are just a switchboard — no real pre-qualification today. Confirms qualifying on technical fit and routing straight to the sales manager.

callWalk.label: Expansion
callWalk.title: A wide Phase 2+ surface
callWalk.body: Todd lit up on rep-assist ideas: a voice agent (11labs) to populate SugarCRM by phone, photo/voice-to-text for handwritten field notes, real-time translation for China/Vietnam/Malaysia deals, and an IT-triage agent. All genuinely wanted — all flagged 'later.'

callWalk.label: Close
callWalk.title: Verbal go + logistics
callWalk.body: Phase 1 approved, 'keep it simple.' $1,500 via Stripe link or check + 1099. Todd will email the SM the questions today (sees him Wed at the Imagine meeting), gather WordPress + SugarCRM credentials, and intro Zach to the web-dev host for a sandbox.

signalThreads.label: SCOPE
signalThreads.title: Phase 1 must stay boxed
signalThreads.body: Todd's own instinct — 'keep it simple' — is the guardrail. The bigger vision (voice agents, transcription, translation, IT triage) is real and exciting but is Phase 2+. Ship the lead-capture chatbot first; log the rest.
signalThreads.note: Todd said it, not us — reinforce it.

signalThreads.label: DATA
signalThreads.title: The product-dev form IS the Phase 1 spec
signalThreads.body: The chatbot's fields come from a 'light version' of the reps' application-discovery form; the SM defines the 1–2 must-haves. Until that lands, build on contact-info + generic qualification and swap the refined fields in.

signalThreads.label: PEOPLE
signalThreads.title: Field reps are tech-resistant
signalThreads.body: Reps are 55–60, old-school, no calendars/booking links, 'pulling teeth' to update SugarCRM. Phase 1 correctly avoids them by routing to the SM. Any future rep-facing phase is change-management, not a plugin.

signalThreads.label: SPEED
signalThreads.title: 4-hour callback = a metric worth owning
signalThreads.body: Todd targets ~4h response and has lost deals to slow callback. A close-won/close-loss view on callback speed is a strong data-driven wedge — note for Phase 2.

best.title: Fast path — live in ~1 week
best.body: Todd emails the SM the questions today; SM answers around Wed's Imagine meeting; credentials + web-dev sandbox land this week. Build starts immediately; $1,500 paid.
best.note: Everything Todd committed to lands on time.

base.title: Staged — live in ~1.5–2 weeks
base.body: SM input trickles in after Wed. Zach ships the contact-info + generic qualification flow first, then swaps in the refined application fields once the light form arrives.

worst.title: Access-blocked — ship anyway
worst.body: SM slow / web-dev access delayed. Mitigation: build locally on a contact-info-only flow, push it live, iterate. Don't wait on perfect fields.

riskFlags.label: Scope creep (benign, self-generated)
riskFlags.body: Todd is producing Phase 2/3 ideas faster than Phase 1 is built. Capture them; don't build them. Keep the invoice and the first build to the $1,500 lead-capture chatbot.

riskFlags.label: Sales-manager dependency
riskFlags.body: The final question flow depends on the SM's 'light form' fields. He's traveling; Todd sees him Wed. De-risk by starting the build on generic fields now.

riskFlags.label: Field-rep adoption (future phases)
riskFlags.body: Any phase asking the reps to change behavior faces heavy resistance. Design future work as invisible/assistive or it won't stick.

protocol.label: Zach · today
protocol.title: Send Todd the sales-manager questions
protocol.body: The list is short enough for a 5–10 min SM chat. Todd emails them to the SM today and discusses Wed at the Imagine meeting.

protocol.label: Zach · this week
protocol.title: Send Stripe link + W-9
protocol.body: $1,500, itemized to the Phase 1 scope; provide W-9 / 1099 info so Todd's AP person can process it.

protocol.label: Zach · this week
protocol.title: Get access + a sandbox
protocol.body: WordPress login (Todd's or via the web-dev host), SugarCRM (the SM has access), and an intro to the web-dev company for a lower/sandbox environment to build safely before going live.

protocol.label: Todd · today→Wed
protocol.title: Email the SM + gather credentials
protocol.body: Send the questions today; discuss Wed. Pull together WordPress + SugarCRM credentials and connect Zach with the web-dev host.
